question_text: A 60-year-old man, who was a coal miner for more than 15 years presents with complaints of a cough and shortness of breath. His cough started 6 years ago and is dry and persistent. The shortness of breath started 4 months ago and is exacerbated by physical activity. When interviewed, his physician discovers that he doesn’t take any safety measures when working in the mines. Vital signs include: heart rate 85/min, respiratory rate 32/min, and blood pressure 125/90 mm Hg. On physical examination, there are diminished respiratory sounds on both sides. In his chest X-ray, interstitial fibrosis with reticulonodular infiltrate with honeycombing is found on both sides. What is the most likely diagnosis?
